headline: Malaysia's Diabetes Rate Dipped in 2023; the Obesity Driving It Kept Climbing
context: The 2023 National Health and Morbidity Survey put adult diabetes at 15.6%, down from 18.3% in 2019. In the same survey, the share of adults overweight or obese rose to 54.4%, its third straight rise since 2011's 44.5%.

changes.summary: Correction: we said 2023 marked the fourth straight rise in overweight and obesity since 2011, when it was the third, and we replaced an unconfirmed figure on unaware diabetics aged 18 to 29 with the survey's own split between known and undiagnosed diabetes.

cards.big: Adult diabetes fell to 15.6% in 2023, down from 18.3% in 2019, and the drop looks like good news.
cards.sub: One survey down is not a trend. The risk factor that drives future diabetes moved the opposite way.

cards.big: Overweight and obesity climbed to 54.4% of adults in 2023, up from 50.1% (2019), 47.7% (2015) and 44.5% (2011).
cards.sub: More than one in two adults now carry excess weight, a major modifiable driver of type 2 diabetes.

cards.big: Nearly two in five adults with diabetes in 2023 did not know they had it: 5.9 of the 15.6 points came from the survey's own blood test.
cards.sub: Known diabetes edged up, from 9.4% in 2019 to 9.7%. The whole fall came in undiagnosed cases, from 8.9% to 5.9%.

cards.big: One in two adults lead sedentary lives, and about 84% take part in no sport, fitness or leisure activity.
cards.sub: Physical inactivity is a modifiable risk factor that feeds the rising weight trend.

cards.big: One year's diabetes figure is a snapshot. Body weight, a major modifiable driver, has risen at every survey since 2011.
Judging the epidemic by one survey is like calling the tide from a single wave.
cards.sub: The waterline that shapes future risk, the share of adults overweight, has risen at every reading.

cards.big: One better year in the diabetes data does not reverse a decade of getting heavier.

sources: NHMS 2011/2015/2019/2023 (MOH/IKU): fact sheet and key findings; CodeBlue; FMT
